newsitem.title: FRANCE: No basis to 50 bln Ffr welfare gap forecast-Barrot.
newsitem.headline: No basis to 50 bln Ffr welfare gap forecast-Barrot.

text.p: French Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot said on Monday there was no basis to recent reports in newspapers that the government was forecasting a 50 billion franc social security deficit in 1997.

A joint statement issued by Barrot and junior Health Minister Herve Gaymard said, "The reports appearing in the press recently referring to a 50 billion franc forecast for the 1997 social security deficit are without any foundation."
They reaffirmed that the forecast for the 1997 social security deficit is 30.4 billion francs.

The statement said it was true the latest forecast for 1997 wage growth from the national accounts commission was 2.7 percent, lower than the 3.3 percent used in the budget. It said this revision corresponded to a loss of receipts of some five billion francs.
However it said to pretend that the loss of receipts would be in the order of 20 billion francs, supposed a growth in wages of 0.8 percent, "which is very far from all economic forecasts".
